claims.claim: **Bell palsy = a one-sided, idiopathic facial nerve palsy of lower motor neuron type. Rule out other causes before diagnosing it.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Other causes include infection, inflammation, trauma, tumour and vascular events.** Facial palsy that is idiopathic or post-viral is uncommon under 2 years.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Typical Bell palsy:** comes on quickly, over hours or at most 1–2 days; usually mild pain behind the ear or in the face; dry eyes and poor tear clearance.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In Bell palsy every branch of the facial nerve on the affected side is involved**; forehead weakness (and ptosis, as the page puts it) may be evident, and **these are absent in upper motor neuron lesions.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Other neurological features** — severe headache, blurred or double vision, limb weakness or numbness, ataxia — **consider stroke.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Also against Bell palsy:** hyperacusis and altered taste (both uncommon in it), preceding viral infection or head/face trauma, and **severe pain (mastoiditis, VZV).**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A full cranial and peripheral neurological examination is essential**, plus an eye examination for corneal abrasions.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Look for:** vesicles in the ear canal or on the face (Ramsay Hunt syndrome); pallor, hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy (malignancy); otitis media, mastoiditis or parotitis; and **check blood pressure** — hypertension is a rare association — and temperature.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The House Brackmann scale grades severity** and is useful to monitor progress.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The diagnosis is clinical; investigations are not usually required.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **FBE (to exclude haematological malignancy)** if there are features of an alternative cause, particularly malignancy, **or if starting steroids.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If an alternative cause is suspected:** if there are vesicles, swab them for HSV and VZV; neuroimaging in consultation with neurology.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Untreated, nearly every child recovers by 12 months, and most by 6 weeks** — but some have prolonged functional impairment, facial asymmetry and emotional distress. Give the parent handout.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Any child who cannot close the eye needs eye care** to prevent corneal abrasions: **hypromellose lubricating drops a minimum of three times through the day**, and **pad the eye shut after lubricating ointment at night.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Steroids: not enough evidence in children** that early prednisolone improves complete recovery; most recover untreated.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In adults, oral steroids improve recovery — 1 mg/kg/day (max 50 mg) once daily for 10 days — especially if started within 72 hours of onset.** The age at which adult evidence applies is unknown.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Aciclovir may be considered if a vesicular rash is present.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consult Neurology if under 2 years or atypical on history or examination; consult ENT** for otitis media, mastoiditis or parotitis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when there are no signs of complications and GP or paediatrician follow-up within 1–2 weeks is arranged.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Facial weakness and Bell palsy' (Last updated February 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Facial_weakness_and_Bells_palsy/, retrieved 2026-09-23
